events.title: French siege and occupation
hints: A king's engineer besieged a fortress for a month in 1684.
The fortifications were rebuilt by Vauban before a treaty returned the city in 1697.
events.summary: Louis XIV's army captured the fortress of Luxembourg in June 1684 after a siege and held it for 13 years. Vauban rebuilt the defences until the Treaty of Ryswick returned it to Spain in 1697.

events.title: French annexation
hints: A revolutionary army took the fortress after a siege lasting seven months.
Peasants rose against conscription in 1798 in the 'Peasants' War'.
events.summary: Revolutionary France annexed Luxembourg in 1795 after the siege of its fortress, organising it as the Département des Forêts. A peasant revolt against conscription in 1798 was crushed, and the territory was lost in 1814.

events.title: German occupation in the First World War
hints: Troops crossed the border on the first days of August 1914 despite a neutrality treaty.
The steel industry kept running to supply the occupier.
events.summary: German troops occupied the neutral country on 2 August 1914, in breach of the 1867 Treaty of London, and stayed until the armistice. The country's steel and iron industry continued to supply Germany.

events.title: German occupation and annexation
hints: Declared part of a neighbouring Gau after the May 1940 invasion.
Compulsory military service for locals in 1942 triggered a general strike.
events.summary: Germany occupied Luxembourg in May 1940 and annexed it as part of Gau Moselland, banning French and imposing German citizenship. Compulsory military service for young men from 1942 provoked a general strike that was brutally repressed.
